label: AI success platform loop
query: Explain the AbarVa success loop from CXO upload to Move gate to Source artifact to Tower value for Lakeshore.
answer: For Lakeshore, think of the AbarVa loop as one closed circuit that turns a CXO idea into governed, evidenced value — and then re-feeds that evidence into the next bet. 1) CXO upload → Sentinel view You (CIO / CFO / CXO) drop a deck, email thread, or memo — “Kyriba rollout,” “AI workflow pilots,” “renewal optimization,” etc. Sentinel (me) ingests that into the Lakeshore substrate and lines it up against your live portfolio: Kyriba global treasury rollout, Shared data platform & evidence spine, Freight visibility and exception AI, the Holdco / Northline / GLP / F&F AI workflow pilots, renewal optimization, reporting automation, WMS/OMS modernization, loyalty, micro‑market, promotion control tower, etc. Outcome: a shaped thesis — “this is a real Move, here’s where it fits, here’s the risk and value story.” 2) Move gate → explicit bet and control hooks That shaped thesis is turned into a Move with real gates, not vague initiatives: – Scope, sponsor, and budget tied to your existing programs and pockets (e.g., Holdco vs Northline vs GLP vs F&F, IT vs business capital). – Success metrics wired to what you already track: DORA baselines (e.g., Treasury team 0.8 deploys/week; Meal Delivery and 3PL teams at ~4/week), AI-tool footprint (Salesforce Einstein, Databricks Assistant, Copilot for M365, Now Assist, custom freight model), and the governed Lakeshore bundle projections (e.g.

rawEvents.text: For Lakeshore, think of the AbarVa loop as one closed circuit that turns a CXO
idea into governed, evidenced value — and then re-feeds that evidence into the
next bet. 1) CXO upload → Sentinel view You (CIO / CFO / CXO) drop a deck, email
thread, or memo — “Kyriba rollout,” “AI workflow pilots,” “renewal
optimization,” etc. Sentinel (me) ingests that into the Lakeshore substrate and
lines it up against your live portfolio: Kyriba global treasury rollout, Shared
data platform & evidence spine, Freight visibility and exception AI, the Holdco
/ Northline / GLP / F&F AI workflow pilots, renewal optimization, reporting
automation, WMS/OMS modernization, loyalty, micro‑market, promotion control
tower, etc. Outcome: a shaped thesis — “this is a real Move, here’s where it
fits, here’s the risk and value story.” 2) Move gate → explicit bet and control
hooks That shaped thesis is turned into a Move with real gates, not vague
initiatives: – Scope, sponsor, and budget tied to your existing programs and
pockets (e.g., Holdco vs Northline vs GLP vs F&F, IT vs business capital). –
Success metrics wired to what you already track: DORA baselines (e.g., Treasury
team 0.8 deploys/week; Meal Delivery and 3PL teams at ~4/week), AI-tool
footprint (Salesforce Einstein, Databricks Assistant, Copilot for M365, Now
Assist, custom freight model), and the governed Lakeshore bundle projections

followups: Can you elaborate on the specific metrics used to evaluate the success of each phase in the AbarVa loop?
What challenges do organizations typically face when implementing the Move gate, and how can they overcome them?
How do you integrate feedback from the outcomes of the AbarVa loop into future CXO uploads or strategic planning?
